title: Bill Gates proposes major limits on AI development
content:
Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates argued on Wednesday that artificial intelligence needs significant limits or else the harm to humans will outweigh any potential good.
“AI will either be the greatest equalizer ever invented, or the worst source of injustice,” he said in a 6,000-word essay, entitled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.”
            Gates isn’t the first tech leader to raise concerns about rapid advancements in AI. But his essay adds to growing worries about the actions of some AI models and potential job losses, even as the AI companies and Wall Street press full speed ahead on the technology.
    
Gates became one of the richest people on the planet as a key player during last century’s personal computer revolution. However, he wrote that he believes the next technology revolution – AI – will be far more disruptive to society.
“Even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history,” he said, adding that “I don’t see evidence that leaders, experts, and communities are confronting the challenges adequately. There is no plan to ease the entry into the AI era.”
AI can provide great benefits in field like agriculture and medicine, he argued, such as breakthroughs in preventing and treating diseases.
But he also noted that the transition carries big risks, like widespread unemployment, harming the educational and social development of children, or making it easier for criminals and bad actors – or AI itself – to cause deliberate harm.
“As the models become more powerful, they could begin to act against our interests and we could lose control,” he warned.
These significant risks must be controlled quickly, Gates said.
“If someone had a credible plan for slowing down AI advances globally, I would likely support it,” he wrote. “However, I don’t think that’s going to happen. The geopolitical and economic incentives are pushing too hard to go full speed ahead.”
In an interview with CNN’s Anderson Cooper that will air on Wednesday evening, Gates said AI models have gotten dramatically more powerful at a rate faster than he expected.
“They’re now capable of causing cyberattack risk, bioterrorism risk, psychosocial risk,” he said. “I have to say I’m kind of shocked that the exact criteria that we review these models with, and the actions we take to minimize the harms, are really completely missing.”
In his essay, Gates proposed taxing AI or robots the way you would pay a human employee’s payroll tax in order to slow the shift away from using human labor. He also wants to set aside some work to be done by humans only.
“My message to leaders is: You have a chance to act now, before unemployment rises sharply, communities are hurting, and public trust has eroded,” he said. “You can make sure AI benefits everyone. And you can work with other governments to meet this national and global challenge.”

report.summary: Bill Gates urges major AI limits, citing uncontrollable risks and job losses, and proposes taxing AI and reserving human-only jobs.
report.background: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has joined a growing list of tech leaders warning about the rapid pace of AI advancement. In a 6,000-word essay titled "The turbulent AI era is here," he argues that AI will either become the greatest equalizer ever invented or a source of profound injustice. Gates, a key figure in the personal computer revolution, believes this next technological shift will be far more disruptive, potentially leading to widespread unemployment, harm to children's development, and increased risks of cyberattacks, bioterrorism, and psychosocial damage. He laments that current safety reviews and harm-minimization measures are "completely missing." While he would support a credible global slowdown, he doubts it will happen due to strong geopolitical and economic incentives pushing full-speed development. Instead, he urges leaders to act now and proposes concrete policy changes, such as taxing AI like human labor and preserving certain jobs exclusively for people.
key_points: Gates warns that AI's harms could outweigh its benefits unless significant limits are implemented soon. He acknowledges AI's promise in agriculture and medicine but insists the transition will be one of the most turbulent periods in human history, lacking any real plan to ease entry into the AI era.

He highlights concrete dangers: AI models are now capable of cyberattacks, bioterrorism, and psychosocial manipulation. Gates says he is 'shocked' that the criteria used to review these models and the actions taken to minimize harms are completely absent.

To slow job displacement, Gates proposes taxing AI or robots in the same way employers pay payroll taxes for human workers. He also wants to reserve certain categories of work exclusively for humans, ensuring people retain meaningful employment opportunities.

Gates acknowledges that a global slowdown of AI development is unlikely due to overwhelming geopolitical and economic incentives. Still, he appeals to leaders to collaborate internationally and act before unemployment rises sharply and public trust erodes.

His essay adds to growing concerns from tech leaders about AI safety, even as AI companies and Wall Street continue to invest heavily. Gates stresses that the choices made now are critical and that no one is adequately confronting the challenges.
report.impact: Gates' proposal signals a potential shift in how AI regulation might be framed: treating AI as a taxable workforce and legally protecting human-only jobs. For the AI industry, this could mean higher operational costs and stricter accountability requirements, potentially slowing deployment in labor-intensive sectors. Developers would need to build safety review mechanisms into their pipelines, since public scrutiny over unmitigated risks is intensifying. For regular users, the implications are mixed: better AI-powered healthcare and education on one side, but greater uncertainty about employment and increased vulnerability to AI-driven cyber or social manipulation on the other. Gates' prominence adds weight to calls for proactive governance, making it more likely that policymakers will consider taxes, carve-outs, and safety standards rather than letting market forces alone shape the AI era. The lack of a global consensus, however, means these safeguards may be fragmented and slow to materialize.
report.tools: For readers interested in AI safety and governance, watch frameworks like Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy and OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, which outline how leading labs assess catastrophic risks. Open-source evaluation tools such as EleutherAI's LM Evaluation Harness and the AI Risk and Vulnerability Alliance's red-teaming resources can help researchers test models for harmful behaviors before public release.
